name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits; satellite warning
summary: Kremlin dismisses reports Russia could orbit a nuclear-armed satellite from December; Kim visits nuclear sites
state: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on 23 Nov dismissed German media reports that Western intelligence believes Russia could put a nuclear-armed satellite, Sputnik-S, into orbit as early as December; the US Defense Intelligence Agency said in October that Russia was developing such a system (Moscow Times). On 25 Nov Kim Jong Un visited North Korean nuclear material production sites (Korea Herald). No nuclear test, alert-level change or threatened use in an active conflict was found to 26 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: No direct action is needed. In any emergency, follow official UK government guidance.
rubric_hit: Arms-control lapse without replacement and reported space nuclear weapon programme = Watch

sources.title: The Moscow Times — Kremlin dismisses reports about alleged nuclear-armed satellite launch
Korea Herald (Yonhap) — N. Korea's Kim inspects nuclear material sites

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
